human_tolerance.notes: Observed in São Paulo feeding at trees and shrubs in the understory, including palm fruits; the species also uses urban plant resources.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: The species is a year-round resident and is regularly observed in pairs or flocks; a seasonal breeding window is not asserted.

vocalizations.description: A harsh, strident, squawk repeated by the whole flock in flight, so that a passing group sounds continuous.
A sharp, excited screeching given when the flock is disturbed or mobbing a predator.

taxonomy.note: GBIF Backbone Taxonomy gives Aves Psittaciformes Psittacidae and the authorship on the matched name; the Wikidata item confirms the English common name.

external.note: GBIF usage key 2479562 and iNaturalist taxon id 19214 as matched by the GBIF backbone and the iNaturalist taxa API; Wikidata Q1086851 carries the same identifiers.

common_names.note: English common name from Wikidata; Portuguese name from the article's interlanguage links.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern for Plain parakeet.

range.note: Wikipedia: endemic to Brazil, ranging from Bahia to Parana and as far inland as Goias. Native range listed as BR.

traits.body_plan.note: A perching passerine or parrot; biped_winged mesh.

traits.limb_count.note: Two legs; wings are not counted as limbs.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Authored params for the shared perching-songbird program. Climb is the declared non-flight locomotion and has no pose in schema/v0.1/body-plans.json, so no climb pose is declared; a long flee distance suits a flock that flushes together.

traits.metamorphosis.note: None; the young hatch as fledged nestlings.

traits.senses.note: Colour vision in all birds; hearing and olfaction values are authored judgement, as no open source quantifies them here.

traits.nest_type.note: The broad Cavity category is retained from the existing species description as a model choice. No verified primary source reviewed here supports communal nesting or termite nests for this species, so those claims are removed.

traits.mass_kg.note: AVONET Mass 63 g; Wikipedia gives about 63 g.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits 1.0 gives a global species-level diet allocation (fruit 30%, seed 30%, plant-other 30%, invertebrate 10%; plant-other mapped to browse). A São Paulo campus study independently documents plant-heavy feeding on seeds, fruit and nectar. The global proportions remain dataset values, not local percentages.

traits.social.note: Portuguese Wikipedia: gregarious, flocks of 15-20 birds with larger flocks of up to 100 not unusual. group_size [2, 20] uses the typical flock as the upper bound.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal 0 (diurnal); Plain parakeet describes daytime activity.

traits.defense.note: Authored: flies to cover when disturbed.

traits.wariness.note: Authored. Bold and noisy in city parks and streets, so set low.

habitat.use.note: The field study directly reports feeding at a palm tree and carrying fruit to understorey trees and shrubs in São Paulo. Arboreal use is modeled as 1.0; the paper does not estimate a population-level habitat-use percentage.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: roosts in dense vegetation or a cavity.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet. Cavity is a broad nesting category; no communal or termite-nest claim is made. Perch weight is a simulation judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: The São Paulo campus survey documents urban plant feeding; the species-specific field study documents feeding at trees and understory plants. The garden-tolerance label is an authored simulation classification.

seasonal.strategy.note: A year-round resident of subtropical Brazil with no migration or dormancy described.

seasonal.phases.note: No reliable primary source found for a São Paulo nesting calendar. Year-round residency and flock behavior are modeled without asserting breeding months or nest-site details.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Only life-stage names are retained; durations and clutch-size claims were removed because no primary species-level evidence was located.

behavior.note: The species-local program replaces the shared songbird ground hop with climbing movement. The São Paulo field study records parakeets feeding on and moving around palm fruit-bearing branches. Climb is the authored movement choice for arboreal feeding.

look.note: The plain parakeet is predominantly green, with yellow-green underparts and blue-green/blue-violet flight feathers; there is no orange head or orange bill. General green plumage is also described in the São Paulo field study; palette is a simplified model.

vocalizations.song.note: Call description from the Plain parakeet article; months, time windows, cooldowns and loudness are authored judgement, as no open source quantifies them.

vocalizations.alarm.note: Call description from the Plain parakeet article; months, time windows, cooldowns and loudness are authored judgement, as no open source quantifies them.

traits.lifespan_y.note: A low-precision simulation value for a small parakeet, informed by long-lived psittacids but without a species-specific wild estimate. This is a model parameter, not a field measurement.
